subject: [PATCH v3 1/7] mm: support promotion-only NUMA hinting scans

2026-09-22.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new NUMA hinting scan mode called 'promotion-only' that allows the kernel to identify when a VMA becomes active, without applying heuristics like read-only VMAs or activeness. The patch adds a new flag MM_CP_PROT_NUMA_PROMO_ONLY and modifies task_numa_work() to select the type of walk based on this flag. It also updates folio_can_map_prot_numa() to derive the single-threaded private state at the point of use, rather than adding another precomputed boolean to the protection-walk interface. This change is required for memory-tiering fixes and must be accompanied by them when backported.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that applying normal-mode optimizations to an entire VMA in tiering or combined mode breaks tiering, and confirms this is the reason for adding MM_CP_PROT_NUMA_PROMO_ONLY.
sentiment_signals: confirmed the purpose of a patch

2026-09-24.patch_summary: This patch introduces support for promotion-only NUMA hinting scans in the Linux kernel. It adds a new mode, MM_CP_PROT_NUMA_PROMO_ONLY, which allows tasks to specify that they only want to scan for pages that can be promoted to a higher-tier node. The patch also updates various functions, including folio_can_map_prot_numa and task_numa_work, to use this new mode. This change is intended to improve the performance of memory tiering systems by reducing unnecessary scans and allowing tasks to focus on promoting pages to higher-tier nodes. The patch also includes several other changes to clean up the interface and reduce complexity.
